purpose: Provide an evaluable method ontology for weighing arguments and evidence to reach a justified, defeasible verdict on whether a claim is adequately supported, as session-bounded appraisal work units within a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: the parent domain is Argumentation & Critical Reasoning; this KB covers the claim_evidence_appraisal subdomain only
no observed dataset or benchmark is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
nodes are concrete appraisal/weighing methods, each bounded to one heavy reasoning session
the appraiser has access to the argument text and its cited evidence
exclusions: discovery and retrieval of the evidence itself (covered by sibling retrieval subdomains)
formal deductive proof theory and symbolic logic calculi
domain-specific evidentiary law procedure beyond general burden/standard concepts
primary data collection or experiment execution

competency_questions.question: Given a raw claim and decision context, how is the claim sharpened and what standard of proof applies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAIM_FRAME fixes claim and proof standard

competency_questions.question: How is an argument reconstructed into explicit premises, conclusion, and unstated assumptions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ARG_RECONSTRUCT outputs an explicit premise set

competency_questions.question: How are premises appraised for acceptability, relevance, and sufficiency (the ARG/RSA triad)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the three triad nodes produce per-premise and joint judgments

competency_questions.question: How is the warrant licensing the inference and its backing assessed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WARRANT_BACKING states warrant, backing, and qualifier

competency_questions.question: How are evidence sources appraised for quality, provenance, and integrity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVIDENCE_QUALITY and EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY rate sources and authenticity

competency_questions.question: How is probative weight assigned and combined across convergent or cumulative evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROBATIVE_WEIGHT and CONVERGE_CUMUL produce an aggregate weight

competency_questions.question: How are rebutting and undercutting defeaters identified and resolved?
How are argumentation-scheme critical questions and fallacy checks applied to test an argument?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCHEME_CQ and FALLACY_BIAS_SCREEN run structured tests

competency_questions.question: How are burden of proof, presumption, and burden-shifting managed?
How are rival explanations compared on explanatory virtues to pick the best?
How are competing or conflicting arguments adjudicated and dialectically stress-tested?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETING_ADJUDICATE and DIALECTIC_TEST compare both sides

competency_questions.question: How does the appraisal reach a verdict when the burden or proof standard is decisive rather than the evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BURDEN_PRESUMPTION and VERDICT_SYNTH apply the standard

competency_questions.question: How is residual uncertainty quantified and the verdict's robustness to assumptions tested?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNCERTAINTY_QUANT and SENSITIVITY_ROBUST report confidence and flip-points

competency_questions.question: How is the appraisal packaged into an auditable, reproducible record?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIT_TRAIL links the verdict to all judgments

glossary.definition: a single testable proposition whose support is to be appraised
a set of premises offered in support of a conclusion
whether a premise is credible on its own grounds to a reasonable audience
whether a premise bears on the acceptability of the conclusion
whether accepted relevant premises provide enough grounds for the standard of proof
the inferential license carrying grounds to a claim (Toulmin)
the graded inferential force by which evidence shifts belief in a claim
a consideration giving direct reason against the conclusion
a consideration that severs the link between grounds and conclusion without disproving it
the obligation on a party to provide sufficient support for its claim
a scheme-specific probe whose unanswered status defeats a presumptive argument
selecting the hypothesis that best explains the evidence on explanatory virtues
a justified judgment that can be overturned by specified future considerations

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established argumentation and evidence-appraisal literature (e.g., Walton/Reed/Macagno Argumentation Schemes 2008; Govier A Practical Study of Argument 2013; Schum Evidential Foundations of Probabilistic Reasoning 1994; van Eemeren et al Handbook of Argumentation Theory 2014) and analytic practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Frame the target claim precisely and fix the applicable standard of proof and decision threshold before any weighing begins.
contradictors: claimant who states the claim too vaguely to test

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the claim is reframed, narrowed, or the stakes/standard of proof change

pros.claim: every later appraisal weight is relative to the fixed proof standard
pros.example: a 'beyond reasonable doubt' standard rejects evidence a 'balance of probabilities' standard would accept

cons.claim: a vague claim makes relevance and sufficiency untestable
cons.example: appraising 'the policy works' without specifying outcome or population yields no checkable verdict

failure_modes: claim left ambiguous so premises cannot be tested
proof standard left implicit and applied inconsistently
acceptance_tests: claim is a single testable proposition
proof standard and threshold are explicit and justified

nodes.definition: Reconstruct the argument into explicit premises, conclusion, and unstated assumptions so its inferential structure can be appraised.
contradictors: rhetorician who treats persuasion as proof

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the argument text is revised or a new line of reasoning is added

pros.claim: surfacing unstated premises exposes the argument's real load-bearing assumptions
pros.example: recovering an assumed 'all swans observed are white' premise reveals an inductive leap

cons.claim: charity vs accuracy tension can distort the reconstructed argument
cons.example: over-charitable reconstruction silently repairs a fallacy the arguer actually committed

failure_modes: linked premises mis-modeled as independent convergent support
missing premise invented rather than recovered
acceptance_tests: each conclusion has an explicit premise set
linked vs convergent structure is marked

nodes.definition: Judge whether each premise is acceptable to a reasonable audience given its own grounds, independent of the conclusion it supports.

included: acceptability tests (a-priori truth, common knowledge, testimony, supported by sub-argument)
excluded: sufficiency of the whole premise set

contradictors: arguer who asserts contested premises as self-evident

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a premise's supporting sub-argument or background commitment changes

pros.claim: acceptability is judged on the premise's own grounds, blocking question-begging
pros.example: a premise supported only by the conclusion is flagged as circular

cons.claim: acceptability is audience-relative and can drift with assumed common knowledge
cons.example: a premise 'everyone knows X' is acceptable to one audience and contested by another

failure_modes: contested premise accepted as common knowledge
circular premise accepted because it matches the conclusion
acceptance_tests: each premise rated on independent grounds
no premise accepted solely because it supports the conclusion

nodes.definition: Judge whether each accepted premise actually bears on the conclusion, increasing or decreasing its acceptability.

excluded: whether the premise set is jointly sufficient

contradictors: debater who piles on true-but-irrelevant premises

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the conclusion is restated or a premise's role in the inference changes

pros.claim: separating relevance from truth prevents true-but-irrelevant premises from inflating support
pros.example: a true statistic unrelated to the causal claim is excluded from the weight

cons.claim: relevance is a matter of degree and can be contested
cons.example: analogical relevance depends on which similarities are deemed material

failure_modes: true-but-irrelevant premise counted as support
relevance conflated with probative strength
acceptance_tests: each premise's relevance to the conclusion is stated
irrelevant premises are excluded from weighing
revisit_triggers: inference role of a premise changes

nodes.definition: Judge whether the accepted, relevant premises jointly provide enough grounds to meet the standard of proof for the conclusion.

included: adequacy of grounds vs proof standard
what missing premise would be required
excluded: acceptability and relevance of individual premises
probative weight of single evidence items

contradictors: arguer satisfied by any nonzero support

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the proof standard changes or new premises are added that close or open gaps

pros.claim: sufficiency ties the weighing to the explicit proof standard, preventing under-support
pros.example: two anecdotes are judged insufficient for a population-level causal claim

cons.claim: sufficiency thresholds are judgment calls vulnerable to motivated reasoning
cons.example: a partisan sets the bar low for a favored conclusion and high for a disfavored one

failure_modes: hasty generalization from too little evidence
sufficiency judged without reference to the proof standard
acceptance_tests: sufficiency judged against the explicit proof standard
each evidential gap is named with the premise that would close it

nodes.definition: Assess the warrant licensing the inference from grounds to claim and the backing that supports that warrant, including its scope and exceptions.
contradictors: arguer who omits the inferential warrant entirely

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the domain backing for the inferential warrant is updated or contested

pros.claim: naming the warrant exposes whether the inference is licensed at all
pros.example: a leap from correlation to cause is blocked when no causal warrant can be backed

cons.claim: strong-looking backing can mask a narrow or outdated warrant
cons.example: a warrant backed by a superseded study still appears authoritative

failure_modes: inference accepted with no statable warrant
qualifier strength overstated beyond the backing
acceptance_tests: the licensing warrant is stated and its backing assessed
the qualifier matches the strength of the backing

nodes.definition: Appraise the credibility, reliability, and authority of each evidence source feeding the premises.
contradictors: source who is authoritative in an unrelated field

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a source's reliability, expertise relevance, or conflict-of-interest status changes

pros.claim: low-quality sources are filtered before they can contribute probative weight
pros.example: an industry-funded study with undisclosed conflicts is down-weighted

cons.claim: authority can be misjudged when expertise is outside the relevant domain
cons.example: a celebrated physicist cited as authority on nutrition

failure_modes: appeal to irrelevant authority accepted
conflicted source treated as neutral
acceptance_tests: each source rated for relevant expertise and reliability
conflicts of interest are recorded

nodes.definition: Assign graded probative (inferential) weight to each evidence item: how strongly it shifts belief in the claim, distinct from its source quality.
contradictors: arguer who treats all evidence as equally weighty

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the likelihood of the evidence under the claim vs its rivals is re-estimated

pros.claim: likelihood-ratio framing distinguishes weak corroboration from decisive evidence
pros.example: evidence equally likely under all hypotheses is assigned near-zero probative weight

cons.claim: heuristic weight estimates can be miscalibrated without base rates
cons.example: a vivid but low-diagnosticity testimony is over-weighted

failure_modes: high source quality conflated with high probative weight
base rates ignored when estimating diagnostic force
acceptance_tests: each item's weight reflects diagnostic force, not just source quality
direction of support (for/against) is recorded

nodes.definition: Combine multiple independent or corroborating evidence items into an aggregate weight, accounting for dependence and double-counting.
contradictors: arguer who counts correlated sources as independent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when evidence items are found to share a common source or method dependence

pros.claim: independence adjustment prevents correlated sources from inflating aggregate support
pros.example: three outlets repeating one wire report count as one item, not three

cons.claim: aggregation can hide that all support rests on one fragile premise
cons.example: a cumulative case collapses when its single shared assumption fails

failure_modes: correlated evidence double-counted as independent
cumulative case rests on one undisclosed shared premise
acceptance_tests: dependence between items is checked before aggregation
double-counted support is removed

nodes.definition: Identify and classify defeaters: rebutting defeaters that attack the conclusion and undercutting defeaters that sever the inferential link.
contradictors: arguer who ignores undercutting conditions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new undercutting condition or counter-evidence to the conclusion is discovered

pros.claim: separating rebutting from undercutting clarifies whether to attack the claim or the inference
pros.example: an undercutter shows the test was unreliable without proving the conclusion false

cons.claim: unbounded defeater search can stall the appraisal
cons.example: endless 'but what if' undercutters prevent any verdict from being reached

failure_modes: undercutting defeater treated as if it disproves the claim
relevant undercutter overlooked, inference over-trusted
acceptance_tests: each defeater is classified as rebutting or undercutting
reinstatement (defeater-of-defeater) is assessed

nodes.definition: Identify the operative argumentation scheme(s) and run their critical questions as a structured test of the argument's adequacy.

included: scheme classification (expert opinion, analogy, sign, cause, etc.)

contradictors: arguer who resists scheme-specific scrutiny

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the argument is reclassified under a different scheme or a CQ is left unanswered

pros.claim: critical questions convert vague scrutiny into a concrete, scheme-specific checklist
pros.example: an appeal-to-expert is tested by the five Walton CQs on expertise, bias, and consistency

cons.claim: misclassifying the scheme applies the wrong critical questions
cons.example: treating a causal argument as an analogy runs irrelevant CQs

failure_modes: wrong scheme selected, irrelevant CQs applied
critical questions listed but not actually answered
acceptance_tests: operative scheme(s) identified
each critical question is answered or flagged unmet
revisit_triggers: argument reclassified under a new scheme
a previously answered CQ is reopened

nodes.definition: Allocate the burden of proof, set presumptions, and manage burden-shifting so unmet burdens correctly decide undecided claims.
contradictors: arguer who shifts the burden to evade proving the claim

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the dialogue type or which party bears the burden changes

pros.claim: explicit burden allocation decides claims that evidence alone leaves undetermined
pros.example: an unmet burden of proof yields a default verdict against the proponent

cons.claim: mis-assigned burden can manufacture an unfair presumption
cons.example: demanding the skeptic disprove an unsupported claim shifts the burden illegitimately

failure_modes: burden illegitimately shifted to the questioner
presumption set without a stated basis
acceptance_tests: the burden of proof is assigned with a stated basis
burden shifts are logged and justified

nodes.definition: Compare rival explanations on explanatory virtues (scope, simplicity, coherence, testability) to judge which best accounts for the evidence.
contradictors: arguer who accepts the only explanation considered

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new candidate explanation is introduced or virtue weightings change

pros.claim: comparing virtues guards against accepting the first or only explanation offered
pros.example: a simpler rival with equal scope defeats an ad-hoc favored explanation

cons.claim: the loveliest explanation need not be the likeliest
cons.example: an elegant theory is preferred over a messy but better-supported one

failure_modes: best-of-a-bad-lot: best explanation still poor
explanatory loveliness mistaken for probability
acceptance_tests: at least two rival explanations are scored on the same virtues
the chosen explanation beats rivals on stated virtues

nodes.definition: Adjudicate directly conflicting arguments by comparing their net weights, defeater status, and burden positions to reach a relative verdict.
contradictors: partisan who weighs only the favored side

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when one side gains a new argument, loses a premise, or a defeater changes the balance

pros.claim: net-weight comparison prevents one-sided verdicts that ignore the strongest rival
pros.example: the verdict survives only if it beats the steelmanned opposing case

cons.claim: incommensurable arguments resist a single net-weight scale
cons.example: a moral objection and an efficiency argument cannot be summed on one axis

failure_modes: only the favored side is weighed
mutually defeating arguments left unresolved
acceptance_tests: both sides are appraised on the same criteria
the decisive factor for the verdict is recorded
revisit_triggers: a side gains or loses an argument

nodes.definition: Screen the argument and the appraiser's own reasoning for fallacies and cognitive biases that would distort the weighing.
contradictors: arguer who labels every weak step a fallacy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a fallacy charge is contested or appraiser bias is suspected

pros.claim: screening the appraiser's own reasoning reduces motivated-reasoning errors
pros.example: a confirmation-bias check forces a search for disconfirming evidence

cons.claim: over-eager fallacy labeling can dismiss legitimate defeasible inferences
cons.example: calling every appeal to authority a fallacy ignores legitimate expert testimony

failure_modes: fallacy-fallacy: rejecting a conclusion because one argument for it is weak
appraiser confirmation bias unchecked
acceptance_tests: alleged fallacies are distinguished from legitimate defeasible steps
an appraiser-bias self-check is recorded

nodes.definition: Represent the residual uncertainty in the appraisal as a calibrated confidence or interval attached to the verdict.
contradictors: arguer who states verdicts with false precision

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new evidence narrows or widens the plausible range of the verdict

pros.claim: an explicit confidence prevents binary verdicts from overstating certainty
pros.example: a 'probably true, 70% confidence' verdict signals room for revision

cons.claim: heuristic confidence numbers can imply unwarranted precision
cons.example: a '63% confident' figure suggests a rigor the heuristic basis lacks

failure_modes: verdict stated as certain despite open defeaters
confidence number implies false precision
acceptance_tests: residual uncertainty is stated as a confidence or interval
known unknowns are listed alongside the verdict
revisit_triggers: new evidence shifts the plausible range

nodes.definition: Synthesize the appraisal into a justified, defeasible verdict that states the conclusion, its support, surviving defeaters, and conditions for revision.
contradictors: arguer who issues a verdict without disclosing its defeasibility

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a surviving defeater is resolved or the standard of proof is found unmet

pros.claim: a defeasible verdict states exactly what would overturn it
pros.example: the verdict names the single new finding that would flip it

cons.claim: premature verdict locking can freeze an unresolved defeater
cons.example: a verdict finalized while a strong undercutter is still open misleads downstream users

failure_modes: verdict presented as indefeasible
verdict not traceable to the appraised support
acceptance_tests: the verdict states its support, qualifier, and revision conditions
every surviving defeater is disclosed

nodes.definition: Package the full appraisal into an auditable record linking the verdict back to every premise, weight, defeater, and decision rule used.
contradictors: arguer who reports a verdict with no working

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any upstream premise, weight, or defeater used in the verdict changes

pros.claim: a full trace makes the verdict reproducible and contestable by reviewers
pros.example: an auditor can replay the weighing from the dossier and reach the same verdict

cons.claim: audit packaging can lag behind late changes to the appraisal
cons.example: the dossier cites a premise that was later withdrawn

failure_modes: verdict cited without a trace to its support
decision rules applied but not logged
acceptance_tests: every verdict element traces to a recorded judgment
the weighing is reproducible from the dossier

nodes.definition: Test how sensitive the verdict is to its key assumptions, weightings, and contested premises, identifying which would flip it.
contradictors: arguer who reports only the point verdict

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a pivotal assumption is found to be more contestable than first judged

pros.claim: flip-point analysis reveals which single assumption the verdict actually hangs on
pros.example: the verdict is shown to depend entirely on one disputed source's reliability

cons.claim: combinatorial assumption interactions can be missed by one-at-a-time tests
cons.example: two individually safe assumptions jointly flip the verdict

failure_modes: fragile verdict reported as robust
pivotal assumption left untested
acceptance_tests: the assumptions that would flip the verdict are identified
robustness across plausible weightings is reported

nodes.definition: Verify the provenance, authenticity, and chain of custody of evidence so appraisal does not rest on fabricated or corrupted material.
contradictors: party who submits evidence with a broken provenance trail

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an evidence item's provenance, authenticity, or custody record is questioned

pros.claim: integrity screening blocks fabricated or tampered evidence before it is weighed
pros.example: a document with an inconsistent timestamp chain is excluded from weighing

cons.claim: provenance gaps are hard to detect without forensic access
cons.example: a doctored image passes a casual check but fails forensic analysis

failure_modes: fabricated evidence weighed as genuine
selective disclosure of a partial record unnoticed
acceptance_tests: each item's provenance and authenticity are verified
integrity failures are excluded with a reason

nodes.definition: Stress-test the leading verdict through a structured pro/contra exchange: steelman the opposing case and force the verdict to answer it.
contradictors: arguer who never confronts the strongest countercase

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new strong counterargument is raised against the leading verdict

pros.claim: steelmanning prevents the verdict from winning only against weak opposition
pros.example: the verdict is retested against the best version of the rejected case

cons.claim: adversarial framing can devolve into eristic point-scoring
cons.example: the exchange optimizes for rhetorical wins rather than resolving the claim on merits

failure_modes: verdict tested only against a strawman opposition
exchange becomes eristic rather than truth-seeking
acceptance_tests: the opposing case is steelmanned before rebuttal
each surviving objection is explicitly answered or conceded

edges.why_related: the sharpened claim fixes which argument and conclusion to reconstruct
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligned reconstruction targets the right conclusion
edges.risk_of_conflict: reconstructing before framing the claim wastes effort
edges.example: a vague claim yields a misaimed reconstruction
edges.resolution_rule: settle the claim and proof standard before reconstructing

edges.why_related: the proof standard and stakes set who must prove what
edges.benefit_of_coupling: burden allocation inherits the fixed standard
edges.risk_of_conflict: setting burden before the standard misallocates it
edges.example: a criminal standard shifts more burden to the proponent
edges.resolution_rule: fix the proof standard before allocating burden

edges.why_related: sufficiency is judged against the standard of proof set at framing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sufficiency threshold tracks the declared standard
edges.risk_of_conflict: judging sufficiency without a standard is arbitrary
edges.example: a high standard raises the sufficiency bar
edges.resolution_rule: declare the proof standard before judging sufficiency

edges.why_related: acceptability is appraised over the explicit premise set produced by reconstruction
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clean premises make acceptability testable
edges.risk_of_conflict: scoring premises before they are made explicit misfires
edges.example: an unrecovered premise cannot be appraised
edges.resolution_rule: reconstruct the premise set before rating acceptability

edges.why_related: the warrant is identified from the reconstructed grounds-claim link
edges.benefit_of_coupling: explicit structure exposes the inferential warrant
edges.risk_of_conflict: assessing the warrant before structure is guesswork
edges.example: the warrant is read off the diagrammed inference
edges.resolution_rule: reconstruct structure before stating the warrant

edges.why_related: scheme classification operates on the reconstructed argument
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correct structure enables correct scheme match
edges.risk_of_conflict: classifying before reconstruction misreads the scheme
edges.example: a recovered causal premise reveals a causal scheme
edges.resolution_rule: reconstruct before classifying the scheme

edges.why_related: fallacy screening runs over the made-explicit reasoning steps
edges.benefit_of_coupling: explicit steps make fallacies visible
edges.risk_of_conflict: screening vague prose misses or invents fallacies
edges.example: an explicit invalid step is flagged
edges.resolution_rule: reconstruct steps before screening for fallacies

edges.why_related: integrity checks target the evidence items cited by the reconstructed premises
edges.benefit_of_coupling: knowing which items matter focuses integrity checks
edges.risk_of_conflict: checking integrity of uncited material wastes effort
edges.example: only premises' supporting items are authenticity-checked
edges.resolution_rule: reconstruct to identify load-bearing evidence first

edges.why_related: relevance is judged only for premises that pass acceptability
edges.benefit_of_coupling: filtering unacceptable premises first reduces relevance work
edges.risk_of_conflict: judging relevance of rejected premises is wasted
edges.example: an unacceptable premise is not weighed for relevance
edges.resolution_rule: rate acceptability before relevance

edges.why_related: sufficiency aggregates the accepted, relevant premises
edges.benefit_of_coupling: relevance filtering sharpens the sufficiency set
edges.risk_of_conflict: judging sufficiency over irrelevant premises overstates support
edges.example: only relevant accepted premises count toward sufficiency
edges.resolution_rule: complete relevance before judging sufficiency

edges.why_related: undercutting defeaters attack the warrant identified here
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a stated warrant exposes its undercutting conditions
edges.risk_of_conflict: hunting defeaters without a warrant is unfocused
edges.example: an undercutter denies the warrant's backing
edges.resolution_rule: state the warrant before enumerating defeaters

edges.why_related: probative weight is conditioned on, but distinct from, source quality
edges.benefit_of_coupling: quality-rated sources feed calibrated weights
edges.risk_of_conflict: weighting before quality screening over-trusts bad sources
edges.example: a disqualified source contributes zero weight
edges.resolution_rule: screen source quality before assigning probative weight

edges.why_related: only authenticated evidence may be assigned probative weight
edges.benefit_of_coupling: integrity screening blocks fabricated items from the weight pool
edges.risk_of_conflict: weighing tampered evidence corrupts the aggregate
edges.example: a forged document gets zero weight
edges.resolution_rule: verify integrity before weighting

edges.why_related: aggregation combines the per-item probative weights
edges.benefit_of_coupling: per-item weights are inputs to cumulation
edges.risk_of_conflict: cumulating before weighting items is premature
edges.example: weighted items are summed with independence adjustment
edges.resolution_rule: assign per-item weight before cumulating

edges.why_related: explanatory comparison weighs the cumulated evidence against rival explanations
edges.benefit_of_coupling: an aggregate evidence map enables virtue comparison
edges.risk_of_conflict: comparing explanations before aggregation is unstable
edges.example: the best explanation must fit the cumulated evidence
edges.resolution_rule: cumulate evidence before comparing explanations

edges.why_related: adjudication uses defeater status to discount defeated arguments
edges.benefit_of_coupling: classified defeaters set which arguments survive
edges.risk_of_conflict: adjudicating before defeater analysis over-credits defeated lines
edges.example: a successfully undercut argument is discounted
edges.resolution_rule: resolve defeaters before adjudicating

edges.why_related: burden position breaks ties when net weights are close
edges.benefit_of_coupling: burden rules decide otherwise-balanced contests
edges.risk_of_conflict: adjudicating without burden leaves ties unresolved
edges.example: an unmet burden decides a near-tie against the proponent
edges.resolution_rule: fix burden before adjudicating close contests

edges.why_related: each competing argument's net strength depends on its sufficiency judgment
edges.benefit_of_coupling: per-argument sufficiency feeds the comparison
edges.risk_of_conflict: comparing without sufficiency judgments is hollow
edges.example: an insufficient argument loses the comparison
edges.resolution_rule: judge each side's sufficiency before adjudicating

edges.why_related: the best-explanation ranking informs which competing argument prevails
edges.benefit_of_coupling: virtue ranking supplies a comparison criterion
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring explanatory ranking weakens adjudication
edges.example: the loveliest-and-likeliest explanation strengthens its side
edges.resolution_rule: rank explanations before final adjudication

edges.why_related: unanswered critical questions surface as candidate defeaters
edges.benefit_of_coupling: CQ results seed defeater enumeration
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping CQs misses scheme-specific defeaters
edges.example: an unmet expert-bias CQ becomes an undercutting defeater
edges.resolution_rule: run critical questions before finalizing defeaters

edges.why_related: the leading verdict is stress-tested against the steelmanned opposition
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a provisional verdict is the target of stress testing
edges.risk_of_conflict: stress-testing before adjudication has no target
edges.example: the verdict must answer the best countercase
edges.resolution_rule: reach a provisional verdict before stress testing

edges.why_related: residual uncertainty is computed from the adjudicated balance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the net-weight margin maps to a confidence
edges.risk_of_conflict: quantifying uncertainty before adjudication is premature
edges.example: a thin margin yields low confidence
edges.resolution_rule: adjudicate before quantifying uncertainty

edges.why_related: unanswered objections from stress testing widen residual uncertainty
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stress-test outcomes calibrate confidence
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring surviving objections understates uncertainty
edges.example: an unanswered objection lowers stated confidence
edges.resolution_rule: complete stress testing before finalizing confidence

edges.why_related: the verdict attaches the quantified confidence and qualifier
edges.benefit_of_coupling: calibrated uncertainty shapes the verdict qualifier
edges.risk_of_conflict: a verdict without uncertainty overstates certainty
edges.example: the verdict reads 'probably true, moderate confidence'
edges.resolution_rule: quantify uncertainty before synthesizing the verdict

edges.why_related: the verdict states the adjudicated outcome and decisive factor
edges.benefit_of_coupling: adjudication supplies the verdict's substance
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesizing before adjudication produces an ungrounded verdict
edges.example: the verdict names the deciding argument
edges.resolution_rule: adjudicate before synthesizing the verdict

edges.why_related: the verdict answers the exact framed claim against its standard
edges.benefit_of_coupling: verdict scope matches the framed claim
edges.risk_of_conflict: a verdict not matched to the claim is non-responsive
edges.example: the verdict addresses the original proposition
edges.resolution_rule: keep the framed claim fixed through to the verdict

edges.why_related: robustness testing perturbs the assumptions behind the synthesized verdict
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a stated verdict is the baseline for sensitivity
edges.risk_of_conflict: sensitivity analysis without a verdict has no baseline
edges.example: flipping one assumption overturns the verdict
edges.resolution_rule: synthesize the verdict before sensitivity testing

edges.why_related: the audit record packages the finalized verdict and its derivation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a complete verdict is the object of the audit trail
edges.risk_of_conflict: auditing before the verdict packages an incomplete record
edges.example: the dossier traces the verdict to its premises
edges.resolution_rule: finalize the verdict before packaging the audit trail

edges.why_related: the sensitivity report is filed in the auditable record
edges.benefit_of_coupling: robustness findings belong in the dossier
edges.risk_of_conflict: omitting sensitivity weakens the audit record
edges.example: the dossier records which assumptions are pivotal
edges.resolution_rule: complete sensitivity analysis before closing the audit trail

edges.why_related: relevance is bounded by the framed conclusion the premises must bear on
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the fixed conclusion delimits relevance
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unfixed conclusion makes relevance unstable
edges.example: relevance is judged toward the stated claim only
edges.resolution_rule: fix the conclusion before judging relevance

edges.why_related: source quality bounds how much corroboration low-grade items can add
edges.benefit_of_coupling: weak sources cannot cumulate into strong support
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating weak items as strong corroboration overstates support
edges.example: ten poor sources do not sum to one strong one
edges.resolution_rule: cap cumulative weight by source quality

edges.why_related: the burden position conditions how much sufficiency is demanded of each side
edges.benefit_of_coupling: burden sets the sufficiency bar per party
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring burden applies a symmetric bar wrongly
edges.example: the proponent must clear a higher sufficiency bar
edges.resolution_rule: apply burden when setting sufficiency thresholds

edges.why_related: pressure to declare sufficiency conflicts with honest residual uncertainty
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balancing both prevents both overclaim and paralysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: forcing a sufficiency call can bury real uncertainty
edges.example: calling evidence 'sufficient' while confidence is low is inconsistent
edges.resolution_rule: let the proof standard, not convenience, set sufficiency; report leftover uncertainty explicitly

edges.why_related: open defeaters resist closing the verdict the appraiser wants to issue
edges.benefit_of_coupling: resolving the tension yields an honest defeasible verdict
edges.risk_of_conflict: finalizing over open defeaters produces a false certainty
edges.example: issuing a verdict while a strong undercutter is unresolved
edges.resolution_rule: do not finalize the verdict until surviving defeaters are disclosed or resolved

edges.why_related: unanswered steelman objections conflict with declaring the verdict settled
edges.benefit_of_coupling: resolving the tension forces the verdict to answer the best case
edges.risk_of_conflict: declaring victory over a strawman inflates the verdict
edges.example: claiming the verdict 'won' while a steelman objection stands
edges.resolution_rule: require every surviving steelman objection to be answered or conceded before finalizing

edges.why_related: high source authority tempts over-weighting beyond actual diagnostic force
edges.benefit_of_coupling: separating the two keeps weight tied to diagnosticity
edges.risk_of_conflict: letting authority drive weight inflates non-diagnostic evidence
edges.example: a prestigious but non-diagnostic source weighed heavily
edges.resolution_rule: weight by diagnostic force; treat source quality only as a gate, not a multiplier

edges.why_related: relevance testing and scheme critical questions both probe inferential fit
edges.benefit_of_coupling: running both deduplicates overlapping relevance checks
edges.risk_of_conflict: duplicating the relevance probe wastes effort
edges.example: a relevance CQ overlaps a generic relevance test
edges.resolution_rule: share results between relevance and scheme CQ checks to avoid duplication

conflict_axes.trigger: a decision is demanded while evidence sits near the sufficiency threshold
resolution_order: apply the declared proof standard to the sufficiency call
record residual uncertainty separately from the sufficiency verdict
escalate if the call sits exactly at the threshold
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the declared proof standard decides sufficiency; residual uncertainty is reported, never used to fake sufficiency
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: sufficiency and confidence point to opposite verdicts
conflict_axes.example: evidence narrowly clears a balance-of-probabilities bar but confidence is only moderate

conflict_axes.trigger: a verdict is wanted while a strong defeater remains unresolved
resolution_order: assess whether the defeater is rebutting or undercutting
attempt reinstatement or resolution
if unresolved, issue a defeasible verdict disclosing the open defeater
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: unresolved strong defeaters dominate; the verdict must remain defeasible and disclose them
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a strong undercutter cannot be reinstated against
conflict_axes.example: a reliability undercutter on the key study remains open at verdict time

conflict_axes.trigger: a highly authoritative source offers low-diagnosticity evidence
resolution_order: use source quality only as an admissibility gate
assign weight strictly by diagnostic force
flag any authority-driven weight inflation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: diagnostic force dominates weight assignment; authority gates admissibility but does not multiply weight
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: weight is being driven by prestige rather than diagnosticity
conflict_axes.example: a famous expert's off-topic opinion treated as strong evidence

conflict_axes.trigger: a charitable reconstruction would silently repair a real fallacy
resolution_order: reconstruct the argument as actually given
note any charitable repair explicitly as a separate variant
screen the as-given version for fallacies
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: faithful accuracy dominates; charity is allowed only as an explicitly labeled separate reconstruction
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the verdict depends on whether the charitable or literal reading is used
conflict_axes.example: adding a missing premise that converts an invalid argument into a valid one without flagging it

conflict_axes.trigger: a decision deadline forces closure before defeater search is exhausted
resolution_order: bound the defeater search by materiality and stakes
issue a provisional defeasible verdict
schedule revisit on the named open conditions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for high-stakes or irreversible claims, thoroughness dominates; otherwise a bounded provisional verdict is issued with revisit conditions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: stakes are high and material defeaters remain unexamined
conflict_axes.example: a deadline forces a verdict before the strongest counterargument is fully tested

conflict_axes.trigger: the evidential balance is near-tie but the burden default points one way
resolution_order: check whether evidence decisively favors a side
if near-tie, apply the burden default
record that the burden, not the evidence, decided
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: decisive evidence dominates; only at a genuine near-tie does the burden default decide
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a verdict rests entirely on the burden default
conflict_axes.example: a 50-50 evidential split resolved against the party bearing the burden

conflict_axes.trigger: many corroborating items may share one upstream source
resolution_order: trace each item to its origin
collapse items that share a common source
cumulate only genuinely independent support
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: verified independence dominates raw corroboration count; dependent items are merged before cumulation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the cumulative case relies on apparently many but actually one source
conflict_axes.example: five reports all tracing to a single press release counted as five

conflict_axes.trigger: the most elegant explanation has weaker direct evidential support
resolution_order: score explanations on virtues and on evidential support separately
prefer the explanation that is both lovely and likely
if they diverge, let evidential support dominate for factual claims
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for factual verdicts, evidential probability dominates explanatory loveliness when the two diverge
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an elegant but poorly supported explanation is being adopted
conflict_axes.example: a parsimonious theory chosen over a better-evidenced but messier rival

edge_cases.trigger: a premise is accepted because it restates the conclusion
edge_cases.example: 'the policy is fair because it treats everyone fairly'
edge_cases.detection_method: check each premise for independence from the conclusion
resolution: require independent grounds or drop the premise

edge_cases.trigger: a true but irrelevant premise is counted as support
edge_cases.failure_mode: relevance conflated with truth, support inflated
edge_cases.example: a correct but unrelated statistic cited for a causal claim
edge_cases.detection_method: test each premise's bearing on the exact conclusion

edge_cases.trigger: sufficiency declared from too little evidence
edge_cases.failure_mode: hasty generalization meeting an implicit low bar
edge_cases.example: a population claim from two anecdotes
edge_cases.detection_method: compare evidence quantity to the declared proof standard
resolution: raise the sufficiency bar to the standard
name the evidential gap to be filled

edge_cases.trigger: an undercutting defeater is treated as disproving the claim
edge_cases.example: 'the test was unreliable, so the claim is false'
edge_cases.detection_method: classify each defeater as rebutting or undercutting
resolution: restate its effect on inference vs conclusion

edge_cases.trigger: source authority drives weight beyond diagnostic force
edge_cases.example: an off-topic expert opinion weighed heavily
edge_cases.detection_method: compare assigned weight to estimated likelihood ratio

edge_cases.example: three outlets repeating one wire report
edge_cases.detection_method: trace items to origins and check shared dependence

edge_cases.trigger: burden illegitimately shifted to the questioner
edge_cases.failure_mode: unsupported claim defended by demanding disproof
edge_cases.example: 'prove it isn't true' for an unsupported assertion
edge_cases.detection_method: check that the proponent bears the burden for the positive claim
resolution: restore the burden to the proponent

edge_cases.trigger: a conclusion rejected because one supporting argument is fallacious
edge_cases.failure_mode: fallacy-fallacy: throwing out a possibly-true conclusion
edge_cases.example: dismissing a true claim because one argument for it begs the question
edge_cases.detection_method: separate argument quality from conclusion truth-value
resolution: evaluate other arguments for the conclusion
do not infer falsity from one weak argument

edge_cases.trigger: verdict hard-locked while a strong defeater is open
edge_cases.example: finalizing 'true' with an unresolved reliability undercutter
edge_cases.detection_method: check for unresolved defeaters before allowing lock
resolution: disclose the open defeater and revisit condition

edge_cases.trigger: fabricated or tampered evidence enters the weighing
edge_cases.example: a doctored document with an inconsistent timestamp chain
edge_cases.detection_method: verify provenance and authenticity before weighting

edge_cases.trigger: a heuristic confidence number implies unwarranted precision
edge_cases.example: reporting '63% confident' from a purely heuristic basis
edge_cases.detection_method: check that confidence granularity matches the evidence basis

edge_cases.trigger: the verdict cannot be traced back to its supporting judgments
edge_cases.example: a verdict reported with no premise-to-conclusion trace
edge_cases.detection_method: attempt to replay the weighing from the audit dossier

workflow.objective: sharpen the claim and fix the proof standard and burden basis
entry_criteria: a claim and decision context are provided
acceptance_tests: claim is a single testable proposition
proof standard is explicit
workflow.do_first_because: every later weighing is relative to the framed claim and proof standard

workflow.objective: reconstruct argument structure, warrant, and backing
acceptance_tests: each conclusion has an explicit premise set
the warrant is stated
workflow.do_first_because: all premise and inference appraisal operates on the reconstructed structure

acceptance_tests: every premise rated on acceptability and relevance
sufficiency judged against the standard
workflow.do_first_because: the triad is the core premise-level appraisal feeding adjudication

workflow.objective: verify, rate, weight, and combine evidence
acceptance_tests: each item authenticated before weighting
dependence checked before cumulation
workflow.do_first_because: weighing must rest only on authenticated, quality-screened, independence-adjusted evidence

workflow.objective: run scheme critical questions, screen fallacies, and enumerate defeaters
acceptance_tests: operative scheme identified and CQs answered
each defeater classified rebutting or undercutting
workflow.do_first_because: defeater and scheme testing determine which arguments survive into adjudication

workflow.objective: allocate burden and rank rival explanations
acceptance_tests: burden assigned with a stated basis
at least two rival explanations scored
workflow.do_first_because: burden and explanatory ranking feed tie-breaking and comparison at adjudication

workflow.objective: adjudicate competing arguments and stress-test the leading verdict
acceptance_tests: both sides appraised on the same criteria
the opposing case is steelmanned and answered
exit_criteria: provisional verdict and decisive factor recorded
workflow.do_first_because: adjudication produces the provisional verdict that downstream steps quantify and finalize

workflow.objective: quantify uncertainty, synthesize the defeasible verdict, and test robustness
acceptance_tests: residual uncertainty stated
verdict states support, qualifier, and revision conditions
pivotal assumptions identified
workflow.do_first_because: the verdict may hard-lock only after defeater disclosure, robustness, and human review pass

workflow.objective: package the appraisal into an auditable, reproducible record
acceptance_tests: every verdict element traces to a recorded judgment
the weighing is reproducible from the dossier
workflow.do_first_because: a reproducible audit record is the final reusable handoff for downstream use and review

priority_rationale.notes: first leg of the appraisal triad
second leg, filters premises for sufficiency
core sufficiency call against the standard
guards the weighing against fallacy and bias
sets which arguments survive into adjudication
central comparison producing the provisional verdict

dominance_rules.trigger: a faster verdict raises the chance of a wrong high-stakes judgment
dominance_rules.rule: rigor dominates speed for high-risk or irreversible claims
dominance_rules.required_action: slow down and complete defeater and robustness testing
dominance_rules.example: skipping defeater analysis to hit a deadline on a high-stakes claim

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node depends on an unfinished prerequisite
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the prerequisite before the dependent node

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise score is offered without eligible evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade unsupported values to heuristic and widen intervals
dominance_rules.example: reporting a 0.63 confidence as if measured

dominance_rules.trigger: an item is high-weight but of unverified provenance
dominance_rules.example: a compelling but unverifiable leaked document

dominance_rules.trigger: an authoritative source offers low-diagnosticity evidence
dominance_rules.rule: diagnostic force dominates source authority in weight assignment
dominance_rules.required_action: weight by likelihood ratio, gate by authority
dominance_rules.example: a famous name cited on an off-topic claim

dominance_rules.trigger: a strong defeater is open at verdict time
dominance_rules.rule: unresolved strong defeaters dominate the urge to close
dominance_rules.required_action: issue a defeasible verdict disclosing the open defeater

dominance_rules.trigger: a desired verdict tempts lowering the sufficiency bar
dominance_rules.rule: the declared proof standard dominates convenient sufficiency
dominance_rules.required_action: hold sufficiency to the declared standard
dominance_rules.example: calling two anecdotes sufficient for a population claim

dominance_rules.trigger: risk, irreversibility, or fabricated-evidence risk crosses threshold
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation above the risk/irreversibility thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: route the verdict to human review before lock
dominance_rules.example: auto-finalizing a verdict resting on possibly fabricated evidence

dominance_rules.trigger: a charitable reconstruction would hide a real fallacy
dominance_rules.rule: faithful accuracy dominates; charity only as a labeled variant
dominance_rules.required_action: reconstruct as-given and screen that version
dominance_rules.example: silently adding a premise that rescues an invalid argument

dominance_rules.trigger: robustness or traceability checks are incomplete
dominance_rules.rule: QA completion dominates locking the verdict
dominance_rules.required_action: block hard lock until robustness and traceability pass
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking before sensitivity analysis is done

dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict element has no recorded supporting judgment
dominance_rules.required_action: add the supporting trace or remove the claim
dominance_rules.example: a verdict factor with no premise behind it

dominance_rules.trigger: many corroborating items may share one source
dominance_rules.rule: verified independence dominates raw corroboration count
dominance_rules.example: counting five copies of one report as five

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the claim and proof standard before any weighing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: weighing against an unfixed claim forces a full redo
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: weights change after the claim is reframed
anti_rework_rules.example: scoring evidence before the claim is sharpened

anti_rework_rules.rule: reconstruct the argument before appraising premises or warrant
anti_rework_rules.rationale: appraising implicit structure causes rework when structure changes
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: premise ratings revised after a missing premise is recovered
anti_rework_rules.example: rating premises that were never made explicit

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the acceptability-relevance-sufficiency triad before adjudication
anti_rework_rules.rationale: adjudicating un-appraised arguments inverts the work order
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: adjudication redone after a premise is found unacceptable
anti_rework_rules.example: comparing arguments before judging their premises

anti_rework_rules.rule: authenticate evidence before assigning probative weight
anti_rework_rules.rationale: weighting fabricated evidence corrupts the whole aggregate
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: aggregate recomputed after an item is found inauthentic
anti_rework_rules.example: weighting a document with unchecked provenance

anti_rework_rules.rule: check source independence before cumulating evidence
anti_rework_rules.rationale: double-counted support must be unwound, redoing aggregation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: aggregate shrinks after a shared source is found

anti_rework_rules.rule: enumerate and classify defeaters before synthesizing the verdict
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a verdict issued before defeater search is revised when defeaters appear
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: verdict reopened after an undercutter is found
anti_rework_rules.example: finalizing before checking for undercutting conditions

anti_rework_rules.rule: run scheme critical questions before finalizing defeaters
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unanswered CQs surface as new defeaters and force re-analysis
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: defeater list grows after CQs are run late
anti_rework_rules.example: skipping the expert-bias CQ then re-opening defeaters

anti_rework_rules.rule: allocate burden before adjudicating close contests
anti_rework_rules.rationale: un-allocated burden leaves near-ties unresolved and re-adjudicated
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a tie re-decided after burden is finally assigned
anti_rework_rules.example: adjudicating a 50-50 split with no burden rule

anti_rework_rules.rule: steelman and answer the opposition before locking the verdict
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a verdict that only beat a strawman is overturned later
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: verdict revised after a strong countercase appears
anti_rework_rules.example: declaring victory over a weak version of the opposition

anti_rework_rules.rule: run sensitivity analysis before hard-locking the verdict
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a fragile verdict hard-locked must be unwound on any assumption change
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: verdict flips when one assumption is perturbed post-lock

anti_rework_rules.rule: build the audit trace before handing off the verdict
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an untraceable verdict cannot be reviewed and is re-derived
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: reviewer cannot reproduce the verdict from the dossier
anti_rework_rules.example: handing off a verdict with no working

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or appraisal review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk and downstream impact
action: score defects by risk and coupling
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling or locked node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the defect identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is queued for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to owning subsystem
acceptance_tests: defect's owning subsystem applied a fix
all derived fields match formulas within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence shifts a node's weight or defeater status
iteration_protocol.detection: compare new posterior to prior beyond delta
acceptance_tests: posterior change exceeds revisit delta only when warranted

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changed a locked or high-coupling component
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream judgment used by the verdict changed
iteration_protocol.detection: detect changed upstream node referenced by verdict
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change are downgraded

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk, irreversibility, or fabrication risk crosses threshold
acceptance_tests: human review recorded before lock

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new appraisal version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version's verdict and traces
acceptance_tests: no unexplained verdict regression

human_review_required_for: claiming a verdict over an unresolved strong defeater

checks.repair_action: modeled sufficiency-vs-uncertainty and authority-vs-diagnosticity tensions as conflict edges, not dependencies
recomputed all derived fields via formula script

test_cases.input_summary: two rival explanations of the same data

expected_properties: authority used only as a gate

change_triggers: a defeater is found or defeated
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked verdict change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream judgment changes
downgrade when an evidence label or weight is revised
